title: The Mediterranean Diet May Work Through Tiny Mitochondrial Proteins
hook: The Mediterranean diet's heart and brain benefits may run through tiny proteins made inside your cells' mitochondria — and olive oil, fish, and legumes seem to boost them most.
key_points: The Mediterranean diet may influence aging partly through small proteins produced inside mitochondria, the cell's energy centers.
Older adults who followed the diet most closely had higher levels of two such proteins, humanin and SHMOOSE, both linked to heart and brain protection.
Olive oil, fish, legumes, and fewer refined carbohydrates appeared especially important for this effect.
The findings could eventually help researchers design more personalized nutrition plans for healthy aging.
content_html: The Mediterranean diet's reputation for protecting the heart and brain has usually been explained in broad strokes — less saturated fat, more fiber, healthier oils. A new study points to a more specific mechanism: tiny proteins made inside mitochondria, the energy-producing structures in our cells.
extra_html: As ScienceDaily reports, older adults who followed the Mediterranean diet most closely had higher levels of two mitochondria-derived proteins, humanin and SHMOOSE, both of which have been linked to protecting the heart and brain. Olive oil, fish, legumes, and fewer refined carbohydrates appeared especially tied to the effect. It's an early finding rather than a reason to overhaul anything — the practical advice (eat more like this) doesn't change — but it gives researchers a more precise biological thread to pull on for personalizing nutrition advice down the line.

related.title: A Longevity Diet That Helped Mice Eat More and Lose Fat
related.hook: A modified Mediterranean-style diet, low in protein but with just enough of one amino acid, methionine, helped mice live healthier, leaner lives — and human data hints at a similar link.

related.title: Keeping Your Brain Healthy
related.hook: No pill prevents dementia, but the habits that protect your heart turn out to protect your brain too.
